driving_question: Can a fictional character serve as the anchor-form that stabilizes a self-conjured entity across a decade - is the fiction the checksum that keeps the conjuration legible in the subject's reality, or the prison the entity is trying to escape?
best_collision: c02070 vs c02013 (Campagna, presence as prime object of production and policing) @0.5513 complicates: the corpus says the object of control is presence-as-data; the book says the data apparatus is the cover story - the real object is enforced by humans (informants, quotas), and the firms exaggerate the technology to sell it. The machine's 'illusion of control' (c01558, Steel @0.5412) is not a bug to fix, it is the selling state. The fiction is load-bearing.
quote: Soldiers in the West Bank were instructed in 2022 to enter the details and photos of at least fifty Palestinians into the Blue Wolf system every shift and were not allowed to end their shift until they did so. There was no security rationale for these actions. (p.86)
mutation_note: The 4chan frame asked checksum or prison; the book answers sales interface. The fiction that stabilizes the export is the convenience story; the fiction that stabilizes the control is the technology story; the real apparatus - informants, quotas, the fifty a shift - runs underneath both. The machine's model of itself is a product photo. The ghost is a headcount. The count has no security rationale, which means the count IS the security: legibility as production target, the quota the ontology.
